title: How far do free models go on their own?
hypothesis: A free-only profile accepts at least 60% of scout, review and bulk tasks and at least 35% of code tasks.
human_gate: Frank approves publishing any oh-my-starlight pack.

runs_on.why: T1 run. Free models cost no Token Pass but the laptop never runs T1 or higher, so this runs on the Railway worker.

arms.model: opencode/* free models only, via enabled_providers

success_rule: Directional only (design.decision_effect none). Per class, the free profile reaches the thresholds in the hypothesis or it does not. A class that reaches them is a candidate for a 10-per-cell confirmation before the free profile is marketed for it; classes below threshold are documented as needing Token Pass. No paid reference arm runs here; compare with EXP-001 results afterwards, not inside this run.
kill: Token Pass cap is $0 because there is no paid arm; any Token Pass spend ends the run. Directional pilot: stop after 12 tasks x 1 arm (one run per cell, below the 10-per-cell floor), so no result changes routing or marketing by itself. Free-model calls go through the OpenCode endpoint, outside the Vercel gateway key, so only non-confidential lab tasks are used.

next_gate.receipt: lab/results/EXP-006.md class table; draft of the free profile

decision_it_feeds: What oh-my-starlight-free promises, and which classes it routes to Token Pass.

design.note: 12 tasks x 1 arm is one attempt per cell, below the 10-per-cell floor. Directional pilot: thresholds below are not used to market a free profile until a 10-per-cell confirmation.
